title: Merz
medium: Collage composed of cut and pasted paper elements, with brush and red and black ink, on tan wove card
altText: An abstract collage of cut and pasted paper pieces on tan card, with strokes of red and black ink. Scraps of different shapes and kinds of paper overlap one another.

context: Made in 1922 by the German artist Kurt Schwitters, who is associated with Dada. The museum record lists a collage of cut and pasted paper elements with brush and red and black ink on tan wove card, and gives no further description. Schwitters used the name Merz for his collages and assemblages made from found materials.

descriptions.k: This picture is made of paper scraps glued together! Some pieces overlap. There are red and black ink marks too. Which piece of paper catches your eye? Where would you add another scrap?
descriptions.g12: Kurt Schwitters made this picture by gluing down cut pieces of paper. He added red and black ink with a brush. The scraps overlap like a puzzle. He called this kind of art Merz. Which scraps look like they came from something else? What would you add?
descriptions.g35: Kurt Schwitters, a German artist, made Merz in 1922 by cutting and gluing paper pieces onto a card and adding red and black ink. This is called collage. He often used found materials, things other people had thrown away. How do the overlapping pieces create a pattern? What might the scraps have been before?
descriptions.g68: Schwitters made this collage in 1922 from cut and pasted paper elements, with brush strokes of red and black ink on tan card. He used the name Merz for work made from found scraps. Dada artists often turned everyday material into art. How do overlapping pieces, ink, and the card's color create an arrangement, and what makes a scrap worthy of art?
descriptions.g910: Merz (1922) is a collage of cut paper with red and black ink on tan card, a work by Schwitters, who is associated with the Dada movement. The museum offers no commentary, but the method is clear: found scraps are rearranged into a new design. Consider how composition turns everyday material into something deliberate, and how Dada questioned what art should be made from.
descriptions.g1112: Schwitters's 1922 Merz exemplifies a practice of assembling fragments of the everyday into new visual order. The museum records the materials, cut and pasted paper with red and black ink on card, and nothing more, so interpretation must attend to composition and process. Scholars debate how Schwitters's formal sophistication relates to Dada's confrontational attitudes. How does the collage balance chance and control, and what is at stake in elevating ephemera to art?

teacherNote.context: A 1922 paper collage with ink by the German artist Kurt Schwitters in the Art Institute of Chicago. The museum record gives only title, medium and credit line, so a person must review the image, including any printed text. The work is in copyright, so no image is linked yet.
directions: Have students make a collage from clean scrap paper and explain how they chose each piece.
Ask students to find a piece they think was cut from something else and invent its history.
Discuss what makes something art, and whether the materials matter.
